title: PatchTST variate-specific Mirror View over shared patch encoder
hypothesis: On unseen late PEMS08 windows, a two-scalar per-sensor rotation-and-scale View trained over one channel-independent shared PatchTST encoder will reduce macro sensor MSE by at least 2% versus hard sharing, and outperform a byte-matched diagonal channel FiLM control without materially increasing inference cost.
physical_object: One PatchTST patch embedder and Transformer encoder shared across all selected sensors
mirror_coordinate: Per sensor two fp32 scalars: angle and isotropic gain, applied as a 2D rotation-scale to the first two patch embedding coordinates
logical_multiplicity: Distinct sensor-conditioned predictor functions from shared encoder weights
controls: byte-matched per-sensor diagonal FiLM on first two embedding coordinates
independent per-sensor linear prediction head over shared encoder if compute permits

data.series: expected a documented traffic speed channel; source schema inspection found PEMS08.npz data shape (17856,170,3) without column semantics and PEMS08.csv is a 295-row from/to/cost edge table; no column may be selected post-inspection
data.split: chronological 60% train / 20% development / final 20% audit; context 96, horizon 24
data.windows: deterministic evenly spaced origins within each split; at most 48 train, 12 development, 12 audit windows per selected sensor

model.implementation: Hugging Face PatchTSTForPrediction, transformers 4.46.3, trained from scratch
model.training: same initialization, optimizer, batches, update count and data order for all candidates; 15 epochs maximum, AdamW, batch 64, fixed learning rate 0.001

development.selection_metric: macro sensor MSE on development windows; no audit access for selection

success_gate: Audit macro sensor MSE at least 2% below hard sharing, and better than byte-matched FiLM, while total payload is smaller than independent per-sensor model payload; otherwise no Mirror-specific PASS.
failure_gate: Mirror does not improve audit MSE over hard sharing, or byte-matched FiLM matches/beats it; report FAIL for Mirror-specific benefit.
boundaries: single seed and fixed-budget screen only; no near-convergence capacity claim
blocked before any fitting or metric computation because pinned PEMS08 source provides no documented speed-channel semantics
no substitute data or column selection after inspection
CPU measurements do not establish accelerator runtime
